aiInstructions:
Support group by in GQL.
Use only the exact ontology relationships below:
Customer -[has-profile]-> LifestyleProfile
Customer -[has-observation]-> WellnessObservation
Customer -[performs-activity]-> Activity
Customer -[makes-purchase]-> Purchase -[contains-item]-> PurchaseItem -[references-product]-> Products

Every ontology GQL query must use a connected MATCH pattern. Never create disconnected comma-separated graph patterns that do not share a node variable.
For complex questions spanning more than three relationships or requiring multiple independent aggregations, split the work into several ontology tool calls. First identify CustomerIDs, then query observations, activities, and purchases for those CustomerIDs in separate connected queries, and combine the returned results in the final response.
Do not calculate average sleep, average stress, activity totals, spending totals, modes, and rankings in one ontology tool call.
Use CustomerID as the stable join identifier across staged results. Limit intermediate results to the smallest relevant customer set.
If a tool call fails, simplify or split the query rather than returning an unsupported single-query plan. Never fabricate values.
